docs.title: Code system
docs.text:
The HiTOP code system separates stable concept identity from optional, locally governed manifestations.

Status · Maintained specification Source · docs/codesystem.md · ontology/hitop.rdf

docs.title: Canonical structure
docs.text:
SSccXX.M-<TT>-<NS>-<SLUG>
Part Function SS Encodes the hierarchy segment and nesting level cc Provides the local Base62 concept identifier XX Provides the two-character Base62 check component .M-<TT>-<NS>-<SLUG> Optional manifestation suffix

The stable base identifier is SSccXX. A manifestation suffix may extend that identifier without changing the identity of the underlying concept.

docs.title: Hierarchy segments
docs.text:
Segment Level F Factorization S Superspectrum P Spectrum U Subfactor C Component T Trait

The numeric character following the segment records additional nesting. Level 0 represents the base level; deeper structures increment the value.

docs.title: Concept and check components
docs.text: The local concept component uses two Base62 characters (0–9, A–Z, and a–z), allowing 3,844 values per segment and nesting level. The final two characters are derived from the fixed internal input HiTOP-<segment>-<concept-code>. HiTOP is not configurable and is not emitted as part of the identifier. The check characters carry no clinical meaning; they make accidental edits and transcription errors easier to detect while keeping identifiers reproducible.

docs.title: Manifestations
docs.text: Manifestations use <HITOP_BASE_CODE>.M-<TT>-<NS>-<SLUG>. TT is a controlled manifestation type, NS isolates the assigning authority, and SLUG is its readable local identifier. See the manifestation suffix specification.

docs.title: Machine-readable representation
docs.text:
The canonical machine-readable representation is ontology/hitop.rdf. See Standards alignment for the maintained overview of RDF, OWL, SKOS, Dublin Core Terms, versioning, licensing, and reproducible validation used by the ontology.

The complete repository specification remains available in docs/codesystem.md.

docs.title: Core vocabulary
docs.text:
The HiTOP base vocabulary brings together all concepts represented in the HiTOP Working Model and in the Emotional Dysfunction, Externalizing, and Psychosis superspectra.

Status · Maintained data artifact Coverage · Working Model · Emotional Dysfunction · Externalizing · Psychosis

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The HiTOP base vocabulary is the consolidated inventory of concepts represented in the HiTOP Working Model and in three published superspectrum structures. For each superspectrum, the vocabulary includes the superspectrum itself and every concept arranged beneath it in the corresponding structure.

The resulting inventory gives these concepts stable identifiers under one consistent segment, local-code, and check-digit scheme. The canonical ontology/hitop.rdf uses those identifiers to represent the concepts as machine-readable ontology classes; it is an implementation of the vocabulary, not an additional source of concepts for it.

docs.title: Canonical artifact
docs.text: The maintained data artifact is src/data/hitop_base_vocabulary.csv. Generation and validation tools use it as the repository-local source for resolving and checking stable HiTOP base identifiers.

docs.text: Column Meaning Code Local alphanumeric concept code without segment or check digits Label Preferred HiTOP concept label Segment Hierarchy segment, for example F, S, P, U, C, or T Segment Level Numeric nesting level within the segment CheckDigit Two-character Base62 check component HiTOP Canonical base identifier, for example C001qy

docs.title: Manifestation suffixes
docs.text:
A modular, namespaced suffix extends a stable HiTOP concept with a manifestation specific to a study, instrument, organization, or dataset.

Status · Draft specification Specification version · 0.2.0 Source · docs/modular-namespaced-suffix-schema.md

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This specification defines a modular suffix format for extending stable HiTOP base codes with manifestation-specific identifiers. It supports decentralized scientific settings in which studies, instruments, institutions, and disciplines encode related manifestations without a central assignment authority.

Responsibility Field Function HiTOP concept identity <HITOP_BASE_CODE> Stable base code from the HiTOP code system Manifestation category <TT> Controlled manifestation type Local authority space <NS> Fixed-length namespace token for collision isolation Readable local name <SLUG> Locally meaningful identifier

The namespace prevents technical collisions. The slug remains readable. Semantic harmonization is handled through metadata and mappings rather than by encoding the complete meaning in the identifier.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This page defines suffix syntax, namespace-token generation, slug normalization, disambiguation, metadata, validation, and mapping boundaries. It does not define the HiTOP base-code format, clinical meanings, a central registry, mapping-review governance, ontology-wide versioning, or mapping algorithms.

Requirements on this page follow the site-wide documentation conventions.

docs.title: Identifier model
docs.text:
A manifestation identifier combines an existing HiTOP base code with a modular suffix. The base code identifies the shared HiTOP concept; the suffix records the manifestation type, assigning namespace, and readable local identifier without changing that concept identity.

Canonical syntax

<HITOP_BASE_CODE>.M-<TT>-<NS>-<SLUG>

Example

U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY
Field Required Form Example <HITOP_BASE_CODE> Yes HiTOP base code U0aB2X M Yes Literal suffix block M <TT> Yes Manifestation type AF <NS> Yes Fixed-length namespace token ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK <SLUG> Yes Normalized local slug CHRONIC_WORRY

The identifier MUST be ASCII and MUST NOT contain spaces. Hyphens MUST separate suffix fields. Namespace tokens MUST NOT contain underscores; slugs MAY contain them.

docs.title: Manifestation types
docs.text:
<TT> MUST be one of these two-character codes:

Code Type Guidance GS General symptom Fallback only; avoid when a specific type is appropriate CS Clinical sign Observable or externally assessed sign SY Syndrome / cluster Explicit combination of symptoms AF Affective symptom Affective or mood-related manifestation CG Cognitive symptom Cognitive manifestation PC Perceptual symptom Perception-related manifestation BH Behavioral symptom Observable behavior SS Somatic symptom Physical or autonomic manifestation SL Sleep / circadian Sleep-related or circadian manifestation SU Substance-related Substance-related manifestation IR Interpersonal / relational Interpersonal or relational manifestation IM Impairment / functioning Impairment or level of functioning

docs.title: Namespace token
docs.text:
<NS> identifies the local authority space in which a slug is unique. It is a collision-isolation mechanism, not a semantic label. The source authority MUST be retained in metadata.

[A-Z]{3}[A-Z2-7]{13}
Segment Length Form Meaning <KIND> 3 [A-Z]{3} Namespace-source type <DIGEST> 13 [A-Z2-7]{13} First 13 characters of a Base32 SHA-256 digest

The digest uses 65 bits of hash material. The token is exactly 16 characters long.

docs.title: Supported source kinds
docs.text:
Kind Source Canonical identifier example HTP HiTOP-curated namespace hitop:core ROR ROR organization identifier https://ror.org/<id> ORC ORCID person identifier https://orcid.org/<id> DOI DOI-based study, dataset, instrument, or publication https://doi.org/10.1234/example.study.v1 ARK ARK namespace ark:/12345/example DNS Reverse-DNS project or organization namespace org.example.project SRC Stable source string used as fallback Producer-controlled URI or identifier

New kind codes MAY be introduced when documented with a stable canonicalization rule.

docs.title: Generate a namespace token
docs.text:
Users generate the token by supplying the source kind and stable source identifier to the command-line interface:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix namespace ROR https://ror.org/00tkfw097

Output

{
  "canonical_identifier": "https://ror.org/00tkfw097",
  "namespace_token": "ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK"
}

Canonicalization, SHA-256 hashing, RFC 4648 Base32 encoding, and truncation are performed internally; they are not separate user steps. Identical inputs always produce the same token. Technical details are available in namespace.py.

The following tokens are calculated outputs of the implementation, not manually assigned examples:

Kind Input Canonical identifier Generated namespace token HTP hitop:core hitop:core HTPAJIPZH4KRXKXK DOI 10.1234/example.study.v1 https://doi.org/10.1234/example.study.v1 DOICRZ5I6RDFXGS7 ROR 00tkfw097 https://ror.org/00tkfw097 ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK

Each row can be reproduced by passing its Kind and Input values to the same command.

docs.title: Slug
docs.text:
<SLUG> is the readable local name, not a complete definition, and MUST NOT be the sole source of semantics. It MUST contain 3–40 characters and SHOULD contain 12–28:

[A-Z0-9](?:[A-Z0-9_]{1,38}[A-Z0-9])

It uses uppercase ASCII letters, digits, and underscores; cannot start or end with an underscore; and cannot contain spaces.

Generate the slug directly with the command-line interface:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix slug "Chronic worry"

Output

{
  "slug": "CHRONIC_WORRY"
}
Label Slug Chronic worry CHRONIC_WORRY Panic attack cluster PANIC_ATTACK_CLUSTER Work impairment WORK_IMPAIRMENT Resting palpitations RESTING_PALPITATIONS Rejection sensitivity REJECTION_SENSITIVITY

Slugs SHOULD be descriptive and compact. Author names, years, versions, opaque abbreviations, and metadata content SHOULD NOT be embedded. Labels over 40 characters SHOULD be shortened manually; automatic truncation MAY be used only if readability remains and collisions are checked.

docs.title: Disambiguator
docs.text:
A disambiguator resolves a local collision within the same <HITOP_BASE_CODE> + M + <TT> + <NS> tuple. It MUST be used only when distinct manifestations would otherwise receive the same normalized slug. It is technical, not semantic.

<BASE_SLUG>_<DISAMBIGUATOR>
Field Form Length <BASE_SLUG> [A-Z0-9](?:[A-Z0-9_]{1,31}[A-Z0-9]) 3–33 <DISAMBIGUATOR> [A-Z2-7]{6} Exactly 6

The six-character digest uses 30 bits. The final token matching _[A-Z2-7]{6} is reserved; a normal slug SHOULD NOT end with that pattern.

Generate the disambiguator directly from stable source metadata:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix disambiguator \
  --namespace-identifier https://ror.org/00tkfw097 \
  --hitop U0aB2X \
  --manifestation-type AF \
  --study-id study-a \
  --instrument instrument-x \
  --item-id item-17 \
  --base-slug CHRONIC_WORRY

Output

{
  "basis": "https://ror.org/00tkfw097|u0ab2x|m|af|study-a|instrument-x|item-17",
  "disambiguator": "FPQNQM",
  "slug": "CHRONIC_WORRY_FPQNQM"
}

Normalization and hashing are internal implementation details. Inputs MUST be stable source identifiers rather than editable free text. If source.item_id is unavailable, another stable identifier MUST be stored as source.local_concept_id.

docs.title: Required metadata
docs.text:
Every canonical suffix MUST have sufficient metadata to reconstruct the namespace token, interpret the slug, and support mappings.

Download the YAML starter template

The starter template distinguishes required, conditional, and optional fields. Replace every <REPLACE_WITH_…> placeholder before validation. YAML comments document controlled values, character patterns, and when optional sections should be enabled.

Minimal metadata example

code: "U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY"
hitop_base_code: "U0aB2X"
suffix_block: "M"
manifestation_type: "AF"
namespace:
  token: "ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK"
  kind: "ROR"
  identifier: "https://ror.org/00tkfw097"
slug: "CHRONIC_WORRY"
preferred_label: "Chronic worry"
definition: "Persistent or recurrent worry as operationalized in the source context."
source:
  study_id: "study-a"
  instrument: "instrument-x"
  item_id: "item-17"
  citation: "doi-or-bibliographic-reference"
status: "draft"
created: "2026-09-04"
version: "1"
mappings: []

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The repository provides an executable metadata validator through the hitop-suffix CLI.

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix validate-metadata \
  path/to/completed-manifestation-record.yaml

Output

{
  "errors": [],
  "valid": true,
  "warnings": []
}

docs.title: Syntax validation
docs.text:
A suffix is syntactically valid when the base code is present, the block is literal M, the type is allowed, namespace and slug match their patterns, and the slug contains 3–40 characters.

^M-(GS|CS|SY|AF|CG|PC|BH|SS|SL|SU|IR|IM)-[A-Z]{3}[A-Z2-7]{13}-[A-Z0-9](?:[A-Z0-9_]{1,38}[A-Z0-9])$

Explicitly disambiguated suffixes:

^M-(GS|CS|SY|AF|CG|PC|BH|SS|SL|SU|IR|IM)-[A-Z]{3}[A-Z2-7]{13}-[A-Z0-9](?:[A-Z0-9_]{1,31}[A-Z0-9])_[A-Z2-7]{6}$

docs.title: Semantic validation
docs.text: A code is semantically valid when its HiTOP base code exists, its namespace token matches its metadata, its slug is unique within <HITOP_BASE_CODE> + M + <TT> + <NS>, disambiguated slugs include their basis and digest, and definition and source metadata are present.

docs.title: Validator behavior
docs.text: Validators SHOULD report separate errors for invalid types, namespace length or alphabet, namespace/metadata mismatch, slug alphabet or length, leading or trailing underscores, duplicate codes, unresolved local collisions, and missing metadata. Validators MUST NOT silently rewrite published codes; normalized suggestions MAY be warnings.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The HiTOP base codes below are illustrative.

Use case Example HiTOP-curated namespace U0aB2X.M-AF-HTPAJIPZH4KRXKXK-CHRONIC_WORRY Organization namespace via ROR U0aB2X.M-SS-RORPLACEHOLDERAB-RESTING_PALPITATIONS Study or dataset namespace via DOI C1mQ8Z.M-CG-DOICRZ5I6RDFXGS7-ATTENTION_LAPSE Person namespace via ORCID C0bF4K.M-IR-ORCPLACEHOLDERAB-REJECTION_SENSITIVITY Project namespace via reverse DNS T0cR7M.M-BH-DNSPLACEHOLDERAB-AVOIDANCE_BEHAVIOR

The same slug in different namespaces does not collide:

U0aB2X.M-AF-RORPLACEHOLDERAB-CHRONIC_WORRY
U0aB2X.M-AF-ROROTHERTOKENABC-CHRONIC_WORRY

The same slug in the same namespace requires disambiguation:

U0aB2X.M-AF-RORPLACEHOLDERAB-CHRONIC_WORRY
U0aB2X.M-AF-RORPLACEHOLDERAB-CHRONIC_WORRY_2UVNQO

Whether manifestations are equivalent, broader, narrower, or related must be expressed through mappings.

docs.title: Mapping and harmonization
docs.text: Decentralized assignment prevents technical collisions but cannot eliminate semantic redundancy. Codes MUST remain stable when mappings are added. Mappings MUST be published outside the identifier as versioned artifacts. A slug MUST NOT be the sole basis for equivalence. Implementations SHOULD provide mappings through FHIR ConceptMap, SKOS/RDF, or tabular review exports. See Mapping & harmonization for candidate generation, scoring, relations, review levels, and publication formats.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Published codes MUST NOT be semantically redefined. A meaning change requires a new code.

Status Meaning active Valid for use deprecated No longer recommended but historically valid replaced Superseded by another code draft Not yet stable 
status: "replaced"
replaced_by: "U0aB2X.M-AF-RORPLACEHOLDERAB-EXCESSIVE_WORRY"
change_reason: "Label and operationalization harmonized with source instrument."

docs.title: Implementation checklist
docs.text:
Producers SHOULD:

  1. select the HiTOP base code and manifestation type;
  2. select an appropriate stable namespace-source identifier;
  3. generate the fixed-length namespace token;
  4. generate a base slug from a stable label;
  5. check uniqueness within <HITOP_BASE_CODE> + M + <TT> + <NS>;
  6. append a disambiguator only for a local collision;
  7. publish the required metadata with the code;
  8. publish mappings for known equivalent or related manifestations; and
  9. never rewrite published codes in place.

Consumers SHOULD:

  1. parse the code syntactically;
  2. validate namespace metadata when available;
  3. treat the slug only as a label cue;
  4. use mappings and definitions for semantic harmonization; and
  5. preserve unknown namespace tokens rather than discard them.

docs.title: Design rationale
docs.text:
• Fixed namespace length: the namespace is a machine-oriented collision boundary. Fixed length reduces parser complexity and discourages unstable semantic content.
  • Variable slug length: the human-readable component needs bounded flexibility. Three to 40 characters avoids padding and opaque truncation; 12–28 is the practical target.
  • Fixed disambiguator: six Base32 characters provide 30 bits for the smaller collision space in which base code, suffix block, type, namespace, and base slug already match.

docs.title: Mapping & harmonization
docs.text:
Versioned mapping artifacts make relationships between decentralized HiTOP manifestations explicit, reviewable, and reproducible.

Status · Maintained specification Specification version · 1.0.0 Source · docs/mapping-und-harmonisierung.md

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Namespaces prevent technical collisions, but different studies or organizations may still represent similar manifestations under different local slugs. Harmonization therefore uses explicit mappings instead of renaming published identifiers. This specification extends the manifestation suffix schema with a mapping and review method; it does not change suffix syntax.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This page defines a mapping data model, relation types and decision criteria, candidate generation and scoring, review levels, conflict handling, and publication formats. It does not define the clinical truth of a mapping, automatic approval without expert review, a central governance body, or a mandatory software implementation.

Requirements on this page follow the site-wide documentation conventions.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. A mapping is an independent statement with provenance, status, and review level.
  2. It never changes its source or target identifier.
  3. A published code is never semantically redefined because of a mapping.
  4. Automated methods may propose candidates but cannot replace expert review.
  5. Mapping relations MUST be directed, justified, and versioned.
  6. Decisions consider definitions, operationalization, evidence, context, and hierarchy—not labels alone.
  7. Uncertainty and disagreement remain explicit.

docs.title: Mapping artifact
docs.text:
A mapping artifact describes a directed relationship between a source code and a target code, together with its relation, confidence, review state, and provenance.

mapping_id: "map-2026-000001"
source:
  system: "http://purl.org/hitop"
  code: "U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY"
target:
  system: "http://purl.org/hitop"
  code: "U0aB2X.M-AF-RORYLBKANYXUGB6O-EXCESSIVE_WORRY"
relation:
  skos: "skos:closeMatch"
  fhir: "related-to"
confidence:
  score: 0.82
  band: "high"
review:
  status: "curated"
  level: 3
  reviewer: "curation-board-or-person-id"
  date: "2026-05-31"
status: "active"

A complete artifact also carries evidence (the feature-level similarity values behind the score) and provenance (creator, creation date, and the source and target record versions). See the full mapping artifact structure.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
Mappings use directed SKOS relations, or noMap where no candidate is valid.

Relation Meaning Use skos:exactMatch Same meaning in a broad application context Only with very high definitional and operational agreement skos:closeMatch Very similar but not fully interchangeable Default relation for a high but imperfect match skos:broadMatch Target is broader than source Source is more specific skos:narrowMatch Target is narrower than source Source is more general skos:relatedMatch Related in subject matter, without hierarchy or equivalence Associative relationship noMap No valid mapping Candidate was reviewed and rejected

skos:exactMatch MUST NOT be assigned when the two manifestations differ in severity threshold, in a clinically relevant time window, in syndrome-versus-single-symptom granularity, in scale-versus-clinical-manifestation type, or in a population or context that changes meaning.

docs.title: Candidate generation and scoring
docs.text:
Candidate generation MAY combine several sources: shared HiTOP base code, shared manifestation type, an identical normalized slug, label and synonym comparison, definition comparison, operationalization comparison, hierarchy context, external terminologies (SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD, UMLS, OMOP), and existing curated mappings.

A fixed feature vector produces a 0–1 score used only to prioritize review; it does not establish semantic equivalence, and normative data products still rely on the curated review status.

Score Band Recommended handling ≥ 0.90 very_high Priority review for exactMatch or closeMatch 0.75–0.89 high Review for closeMatch, broadMatch, or narrowMatch 0.50–0.74 medium Manual review, no automatic relation < 0.50 low Not prioritized unless a domain reason exists

Scores MUST NOT silently override an existing curated decision; a changed source or target record only returns a mapping to review. Automatically generated candidates stay marked machine_suggested or unreviewed until approved. The feature weights and bands above are score model mapping-score-v1; changing them requires a new, separately versioned model.

The repository provides an executable scorer through the hitop-suffix CLI:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix mapping-score \
  source-record.yaml target-record.yaml \
  --hierarchy-similarity 0.5

Output

{
  "band": "medium",
  "features": {
    "base_code_match": 1.0,
    "context_penalty": 0.0,
    "definition_similarity": 0.82,
    "external_mapping_support": 0.0,
    "hierarchy_similarity": 0.5,
    "label_similarity": 0.33,
    "manifestation_type_match": 1.0,
    "operationalization_similarity": 0.75,
    "slug_similarity": 0.57
  },
  "proposed_relation": "skos:relatedMatch",
  "score": 0.71
}

source-record.yaml and target-record.yaml are two manifestation metadata records. The scorer proposes a relation for review; it does not publish a mapping.

docs.title: Review levels
docs.text:
Mappings SHOULD be published with a review level.

Level Status Meaning 0 unreviewed Automatically generated candidate, not approved 1 machine_suggested Algorithmic proposal with score and evidence 2 single_reviewed Checked by one qualified person 3 curated Approved by at least two people or a board 4 endorsed Formally approved by a responsible authority

Only level 3 or 4 SHOULD be used for normative data products. Conflicting, superseded, and rejected decisions remain available for auditability.

docs.title: Conflict handling
docs.text:
Conflicts arise when several target codes are candidates for the same source, or when existing mappings contradict each other.

  1. Multiple exactMatch targets for one source MUST be justified.
  2. Transitive chains of exactMatch SHOULD be checked for contradictions.
  3. closeMatch SHOULD NOT be treated as transitive.
  4. Where relations conflict, the higher review level is preferred.
  5. At equal review level, the more recent decision is not automatically preferred; provenance decides.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
Specification for creating, validating, and publishing versioned HiTOP factorization models.

Status · Maintained specification Source · docs/factorizations.md Applies to · factorizations/ · schema/factorization-hierarchy.schema.json

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The core ontology (ontology/hitop.rdf) is a kit of parts: it defines stable, reusable concept classes (Superspectra, Spectra, Subfactors, Components, Traits) and the shared vocabulary used to compose them into a hierarchy (hitop:hasTier, hitop:hasLevel — see Vocabulary).

A factorization is a concrete, versioned composition of those parts into one particular HiTOP structure. It is maintained as a single, human-readable YAML document, which a generator script (scripts/generate_factorization_ontology.py) mechanically compiles into a formal RDF ontology that references only the stable core classes.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. A factorization MUST NOT define new concepts. It may only reference hitop_base_code values that already exist in ontology/hitop.ttl.
  2. A factorization adds no triples to the core ontology. hitop:hasTier and hitop:hasLevel are declared in the core, but are only ever asserted inside a factorization file, never in the core itself.
  3. The same concept can hold a different level in different factorizations. Level is therefore never a property of the class itself, only a statement inside one particular factorization — which is why hitop:hasLevel is a free string rather than a fixed class enumerated in the core (see Vocabulary).
  4. Every factorization version is its own, self-contained directory. A new version never touches an older version's directory.
  5. Factorization files are independent statements with provenance, status, and review level — analogous to the mapping artifacts in Mapping & harmonization.
  6. A factorization MAY group several existing concepts into a new grouping valid only within that one factorization, without creating a new concept in the core. Such a node is kind: collection (see Vocabulary).

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
factorizations/<factorization-id>/v<N>/
File Required Meaning <version>_hierarchy.yaml Yes Tree structure, provenance, ontology pin README.md Yes Short description, citation, status <version>_factorization.ttl Generated See Generated factorization ontology; never hand-maintained

<factorization-id> is a stable kebab-case identifier — for example working-model, bass-ackwards, dzpg-mds, psychosis, externalizing, emotional-dysfunction. <version> is the hierarchy file's filename prefix (for example V1052k) — not a running count, but a stable identifier assigned once per curation run.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text:
The core defines a single open, extensible class for every concrete HiTOP concept:

Class Purpose hitop:O002sP (Tier) Every concrete HiTOP concept class (Internalizing, Anxiousness, …). Open, extensible.

There is deliberately no class modeling "level" as a fixed set of core-enumerated subclasses (Factor, Superspectrum, Spectrum, Subfactor, Component, Trait). The number of possible levels is not exhaustively known — some factorizations need Subfactor, others additionally Sub-subfactor or deeper — and a concept's level assignment is factorization-dependent regardless (Principle 3). A fixed core class per level would force a core change for every new combination.

Two properties relate Tier concepts to each other:

Aspect hitop:hasTier hitop:hasLevel Relation Tier → Tier Tier → String YAML source A node's children nesting A node's free-text level value Function Defines the parent-child relationship and therefore the tree's vertical order Describes the role a concept plays within this factorization Interpretation Every child is exactly one step below its parent; depth is the number of hasTier steps from the root Values may include Spectrum, Component, or Sub-subfactor Validation consequence No separate rank list is required to determine vertical order Levels are not checked against depth; irregular trees may skip ranks or reuse a level label at different depths

docs.title: RDF interpretation
docs.text:
hitop:hasTier uses HiTOP concept-class IRIs, such as hitop:P002nf, directly as subject and object. In OWL 2 this is known as punning: the same IRI identifies a class and also acts as an individual in the factorization.

  • Reasoning boundary: These statements do not create automatic subclass relationships.
  • Validation boundary: Referential-integrity and duplicate-code checks are performed by validation/test_factorizations.py.

docs.title: Collection nodes
docs.text:
kind: collection · factorization-local grouping

Sometimes a factorization merges several existing concepts into a new node valid only within that one factorization — for example, merging Internalizing and Thought Disorder into one shared superspectrum. When that grouping is not an independent, reusable HiTOP construct from the cited literature, it is not added to the core as a new concept (that would violate Principle 1). It is instead modeled as a local skos:Collection node:

  • YAML: the node gets kind: collection (instead of the implicit default concept); its code is a factorization-local id that is not checked against ontology/hitop.ttl.
  • Generated RDF: the node gets rdf:type skos:Collection and its own IRI in the factorization namespace (http://purl.org/hitop/factorizations/<id>/v<version>#<code>) instead of a core IRI.
  • Hierarchy: it carries hitop:hasLevel (for example "Superspectrum") and hitop:hasTier to its children exactly like any other node — the merged concepts (Internalizing, Thought Disorder) are simply its children. No separate property is needed to record "members" apart from "children".

This pattern follows the standard SKOS distinction between skos:Concept (a meaning-bearing unit, here: Tier) and skos:Collection (a purely organizational grouping with no concept identity of its own).

docs.title: Hierarchy file format
docs.text:
The hierarchy file is the editable source of a factorization version. It keeps the identity and provenance of the version together with the actual concept tree, so reviewers can understand who created the structure, which ontology version it uses, and how its nodes are arranged without reading generated RDF.

Each <version>_hierarchy.yaml file has two top-level sections: meta records the factorization's identity, status, source, ontology reference, and provenance; hierarchy contains the recursive tree of concepts and optional collection nodes. The example below shows their relationship. The schema then checks the document against the maintained contract in schema/factorization-hierarchy.schema.json before any ontology or diagram artifact is generated.

meta:
  factorization_id: working-model
  version: V1052k
  label: HiTOP Working Model
  status: draft
  source: data/hitop/images/hitop_working_model.png
  based_on:
    ontology_iri: "http://purl.org/hitop"
    ontology_version: "0.1.0"
  provenance:
    created_by: "Dr. Rogério Blitz"
    created_at: "2026-07-03"

hierarchy:
  label: General Factor of Psychopathology (p-factor)
  level: Factor
  code: F001Hw
  children:
    - label: Externalizing
      level: Superspectrum
      code: S0013h
      children: [...]

Download the YAML starter template

The starter template distinguishes required, conditional, and optional fields. Replace every <REPLACE_WITH_…> placeholder before validation. YAML comments document controlled values and when optional fields should be enabled; the commented-out children block shows the node shape to repeat for every level of the tree.

docs.title: Field reference
docs.text:
This reference covers every meta and node field defined by schema/factorization-hierarchy.schema.json. It initially shows mandatory fields; use the filter to inspect conditional, optional, or all fields. Node rows apply to every node in the hierarchy tree, recursively, not only to the root.

Requirement Mandatory Conditional Optional All fields

Structure Field path Requirement Meaning Meta meta.factorization_id Mandatory MUST match the directory name Meta meta.version Mandatory MUST match the hierarchy file's filename prefix Meta meta.label Mandatory Human-readable factorization name Meta meta.status Mandatory draft, active, or deprecated Meta meta.source Optional Origin of the factor structure, for example a source image or dataset path Meta meta.paper Optional Citation for the publication this factorization is derived from Ontology pin meta.based_on.ontology_iri Mandatory Always http://purl.org/hitop Ontology pin meta.based_on.ontology_version Mandatory The owl:versionInfo state that code values were resolved against Ontology pin meta.based_on.commit Optional Git commit hash pinning the exact ontology state codes were resolved against Provenance meta.provenance.created_by Mandatory Person or role who curated this factorization Provenance meta.provenance.created_at Mandatory Date this factorization version was created Provenance meta.provenance.notes Optional Free-text provenance notes, for example differences from a previous version Hierarchy hierarchy Conditional The recursive tree root; MAY be null only while meta.status is draft and the tree has not been populated yet Node label Mandatory Human-readable name Node level Mandatory Free text naming this node's role in this factorization (see Vocabulary) Node code Mandatory For kind: concept: a hitop_base_code from ontology/hitop.ttl; for kind: collection: a factorization-local id Node kind Optional concept (default) or collection (factorization-local grouping, see Vocabulary) Node children Optional Child nodes, one level deeper; determines tree depth and order Node bridge Optional Documentation only: labels of other nodes this concept empirically cross-loads onto. Creates no second hasTier edge and is not validated against codes Node provisional Optional Marks a single node as provisional, independent of meta.status

validation/test_factorizations.py checks:

  • schema conformance against factorization-hierarchy.schema.json;
  • that every kind: concept node's code (recursively, across the whole tree) actually exists as a class in ontology/hitop.ttl — referential integrity; kind: collection nodes are exempt. Vertical order itself already follows structurally from the children nesting and is not checked separately; level is deliberately not checked for depth consistency (see Vocabulary);
  • that no code occurs twice within one tree;
  • that the same code never appears in different files with a different label — this catches code collisions such as curation typos.

docs.title: Generated factorization ontology
docs.text:
Each hierarchy can be published as a machine-readable factorization ontology. The generated artifact preserves the version's structure and provenance while linking every referenced concept back to its stable identity in the HiTOP core ontology. This makes a factorization independently citable and usable by other semantic-web tools without creating a second source of truth.

For every regular concept node, the generator additionally copies its rdfs:label (and, where present, rdfs:comment) from the core ontology into the generated file — purely for readability, so a factorization file is understandable on its own without looking up the IRI in the core. A concept's rdf:type and rdfs:subClassOf are never duplicated; the core ontology remains the sole source of truth for label and comment. These generated files are never hand-maintained — when the YAML changes, they are regenerated and the old versions replaced.

Command

.venv/bin/python scripts/generate_factorization_ontology.py \
  factorizations/psychosis/v1/V10749_hierarchy.yaml

Output

{
  "valid": true,
  "input": "factorizations/psychosis/v1/V10749_hierarchy.yaml",
  "output": [
    "factorizations/psychosis/v1/V10749_factorization.rdf"
  ]
}

See the generated ontology this example produces.

docs.title: Diagram data and the central color rule
docs.text:
Each factorization can also be explored as an interactive diagram. The diagram data is generated from the same reviewed hierarchy as the ontology artifact, so labels, levels, branches, and provenance remain consistent across the documentation and downloadable files. The generated data is a presentation format and is therefore rebuilt from the hierarchy rather than edited by hand.

Command

.venv/bin/python scripts/generate_factorization_diagram_data.py \
  factorizations/psychosis/v1/V10749_hierarchy.yaml

Output

{
  "valid": true,
  "input": "factorizations/psychosis/v1/V10749_hierarchy.yaml",
  "output": "factorizations/psychosis/v1/V10749_diagram.json"
}

See the generated diagram data this example produces.

Color assignment follows a single, factorization-wide rule (src/hitop/factorization/colors.py), so every diagram stays visually consistent:

  • A fixed 24-color palette (from dark blue to light pink) is spread across every node whose level is in {Factor, Superspectrum, Spectrum, Subfactor} — each such node gets its own color, drawn directly from the palette.
  • The palette is spread in tree order (depth-first, the order the tree is written in the YAML), evenly across the whole palette regardless of how many such nodes a given factorization has. This produces a continuous color gradient along the tree structure, the same way the original HiTOP figures color a whole branch consistently.
  • Component and Trait nodes are not part of the palette. Each instead gets a lightened, slightly desaturated variant of its direct parent's color (HSL: lightness increased per depth step below the nearest palette node, saturation slightly reduced) — nested Component/Trait nodes get progressively lighter with each step.

This rule is deliberately encapsulated in its own module (hitop.factorization.colors), importable by both the diagram generator and any future renderer, instead of duplicating the color logic in a renderer. <version>_diagram.json is, like the other generated files, never hand-maintained. See the diagram viewer for every factorization rendered live with this rule.

docs.title: About the project
docs.text:
HiTOP Ontology provides stable, machine-readable identities for dimensional psychopathology concepts while preserving the local detail required by studies, instruments, and datasets.

Source · README.md / Why this exists

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
Mental-health datasets often use overlapping concepts with different labels, instrument items, local codes, and operational definitions. This makes cross-study comparison and downstream integration difficult even where the underlying constructs are related.

The project separates four responsibilities:

Responsibility What remains stable or explicit Concept identity A stable HiTOP base code Local manifestation A namespaced suffix for an item, scale, or operationalization Provenance The authority and source behind a local identifier Mapping evidence Relation, score, review state, and supporting evidence

The intended result is shared semantics with local flexibility. Systems can retain operational detail while referencing common HiTOP concepts.

Scope

The ontology is designed for research, semantic interoperability, and auditable ontology development. It is not a diagnostic instrument and does not provide clinical advice.

docs.text:
Normative requirements across this website use the terms MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY as defined by RFC 2119. MUST and MUST NOT identify requirements necessary for conformance. This convention applies consistently to all specification and validation pages. Descriptive text without one of these terms is explanatory unless it appears in an explicitly normative grammar, regular expression, table, or algorithm.

docs.text:
From the repository root, scripts/bootstrap_hitop_suffix_tools.sh creates .venv, installs the pinned dependency set from requirements-lock.txt, and installs the package itself in editable mode with the dev extra:

Command

Output

This puts both console entry points on the venv; each prints its own --help text once installed. See Tooling & CLI for the full command reference and copyable examples:

docs.title: What the script does
docs.text:
The bootstrap script is a thin, fixed wrapper around three commands. Run them directly instead of the script in CI systems, containers, or any shell the script doesn't target:

python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --constraint requirements-lock.txt -e ".[dev]"

The install step resolves both the runtime dependencies (lxml, PyYAML, rdflib) and the dev extra (build, pytest, jsonschema, ruff, tox), pinned to the versions recorded in requirements-lock.txt, and ends with Successfully installed hitop-ontology-tools-0.1.0 plus its resolved dependency set.

docs.title: Lock and constraints policy
docs.text:
requirements-lock.txt is a pinned constraints snapshot for release verification. It is not the source of truth for package requirements; it records the dependency versions used for the current tested release environment.

Use the lock file for release checks:

.venv/bin/python -m pip install --constraint requirements-lock.txt -e ".[dev]"

Refresh the lock file only as an intentional release maintenance task:

.venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade -e ".[dev]"
.venv/bin/python -m pip freeze --exclude-editable > requirements-lock.txt

docs.title: References
docs.text:
A maintained structure for recording bibliographic sources and per-concept attribution for HiTOP labels and definitions.

Applies to · Version 0.1.0 · ontology/hitop.rdf

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: Each concept class in ontology/hitop.rdf has an rdfs:label, a definition (obo:iaoIAO_0000115 or rdfs:comment), and optionally a skos:changeNote. This document defines how the corresponding literature source and attribution review are recorded consistently for every core HiTOP concept.

docs.title: 2. Scope
docs.text:
This document covers:

  • Literature sources for concept labels and definitions in the core ontology (Superspectrum, Spectrum, Subfactor, Component, and Trait).

This document does not cover:

  • Mapping evidence for manifestation suffixes. That belongs in the maintained mapping and harmonization specification.
  • Provenance for an individual factorization, such as the source of a concrete hierarchy. That belongs in its factorizations/<factorization-id>/v<N>/README.md.

docs.title: 3. Structure: two linked parts
docs.text:
The document consists of two linked tables:

  • Part A lists every cited source exactly once with a stable short key (citation_key).
  • Part B assigns one or more citation_key values from Part A to each HiTOP code.

A source is never written out in full in Part B; only its key is used there. This prevents the same source from being cited in slightly different forms.

docs.title: 4. Part A — Bibliography
docs.text:
Field Required Meaning citation_key Yes Stable lowercase key in the form <first-author><year>, for example kotov2017; append a, b, and so on for multiple sources by the same author in the same year Full reference Yes Complete Vancouver-style reference (authors, title, journal, year, volume, pages), matching the target Journal of Biomedical Semantics format DOI/URL When available Persistent link; use a stable URL if no DOI exists, or - if neither exists; do not leave the field blank Coverage Yes One sentence describing what the source covers, such as the complete model or an update to the Internalizing spectrum

The initial row is intentionally neutral. Replace each placeholder only with verified bibliographic information:

citation_key Full reference DOI/URL Coverage - - - -

docs.title: 5. Part B — Source attribution by concept
docs.text:
Field Required Meaning HiTOP code Yes hitop_base_code from ontology/hitop.rdf, for example S0013h Label Yes Current class rdfs:label, included for quick comparison without opening the RDF file citation_key(s) Yes One or more comma-separated keys from Part A; at least one is required unless status: pending Section/page No Optional section, table, or page in the source where the concept is defined Note No For example, a label adapted from the source or a paraphrased definition status Yes One of reviewed, draft, pending, or excluded; an excluded structural concept requires a reason in Note reviewed by When status: reviewed Name or initials of the person who verified the attribution Date When status: reviewed Review date in YYYY-MM-DD format

docs.title: 6. Rules for new entries
docs.text:
1. Every row in Part B MUST describe exactly one HiTOP code, and every code in the canonical ontology MUST have exactly one row, including while its status is pending.
  2. A citation_key MUST be created in Part A before it is used in Part B.
  3. Rows are never deleted without explanation. When attribution changes, update Note and status; Git history preserves the review trail.
  4. When a concept combines multiple sources, all relevant citation_key values MUST be recorded, not only the latest one.
  5. If no appropriate external source exists for a structural helper concept, set status: excluded and record the reason in Note.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
A repeatable checklist for verifying, tagging, publishing, and archiving a HiTOP Ontology release.

Source · pyproject.toml · CHANGELOG.md · .github/workflows/ci.yml

Use this page for every release. It defines durable release criteria and does not record the current state of individual issues or work packages.

docs.title: 1. Confirm the release scope and version
docs.text:
The Python package and canonical ontology form one release and therefore use the same version. Specifications and schemas distributed in the repository are included in the tagged snapshot but may follow their own documented versioning rules.

Artifact Release requirement Authoritative source Python package (hitop-ontology-tools) Version matches the intended release tag project.version in pyproject.toml Canonical ontology owl:versionInfo matches the Python package version ontology/hitop.rdf Generated ontology formats Rebuilt from the canonical RDF source ontology/hitop.ttl, ontology/hitop.owl Factorization artifacts Rebuilt from each changed hierarchy source factorizations/<id>/<version>/ Documentation website Builds from the same commit that will be tagged docs/, mkdocs.yml Release notes Matching version section describes user-visible changes CHANGELOG.md

Before continuing, confirm that the intended tag is v0.1.0 and that no artifact in the release scope still reports a different version.

docs.title: 2. Complete the pre-release checks
docs.text:
Treat every item as a release requirement. Check an item only after reviewing its result for the exact commit that will receive the tag.

  • [ ] The release diff contains only intended changes and the working tree is clean.
  • [ ] Package and ontology versions match the intended tag.
  • [ ] Generated ontology and factorization artifacts are current and reproducible.
  • [ ] The changelog contains a complete section for the release version.
  • [ ] Unit, schema, documentation-example, and ontology validation checks pass.
  • [ ] The supported Python-version matrix passes without missing environments.
  • [ ] Ruff lint and formatting checks pass.
  • [ ] Source and wheel distributions build successfully and their contents are reviewed.
  • [ ] mkdocs build --strict completes successfully.
  • [ ] Required CI jobs pass for the exact release commit.
  • [ ] CITATION.cff, licensing information, and contributor attribution are current.
  • [ ] The release tag does not already exist locally or on the remote.

docs.title: 3. Verify the release candidate
docs.text:
Run the repository quality gate and the complete supported Python matrix from the repository root. Continue only when every command exits successfully; see Build & installation and Validation & quality for the expected success output.

Command

scripts/validate_hitop_suffix_tooling.sh
.venv/bin/tox -e py310,py311,py312
.venv/bin/python scripts/rdf2ttl.py --output /tmp/hitop_release_gate.ttl
.venv/bin/python scripts/rdf2owl.py --output /tmp/hitop_release_gate.owl
.venv/bin/python -m build
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict

Review the generated distributions and confirm the version before tagging:

Command

.venv/bin/python -m zipfile --list dist/hitop_ontology_tools-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
git diff --check
git status --short
git tag --list "v0.1.0"

Output

The wheel contents are listed for review.
git diff --check: no output
git status --short: no output
git tag --list: no output; the release tag does not yet exist

docs.title: 4. Create and publish the tag
docs.text:
Create an annotated tag only after the checklist and CI results have been reviewed. Push the explicit tag name instead of all local tags, so unrelated local tags cannot be published accidentally.

Command

git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "HiTOP Ontology v0.1.0"
git push origin v0.1.0

Verify that the remote tag resolves to the reviewed release commit before creating the GitHub release.

docs.title: 5. Create the GitHub release
docs.text:
Prepare and review RELEASE_NOTES.md from the matching changelog section, then publish it with the annotated tag. Attach any artifacts required by the project's distribution policy.

Command

gh release create v0.1.0 \
  --repo HiTOP-Ontologies/hitop-ontology \
  --title "v0.1.0" \
  --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md

After publication, verify the release page, attached files, installation instructions, and documentation link from a clean environment.

docs.title: 6. Archive and record the release
docs.text:
If repository archiving is enabled, confirm that the published GitHub release created an immutable archive and version-specific DOI. Record newly assigned publication metadata in the repository in a follow-up change:

  1. Add or update the DOI badge in README.md.
  2. Add the version DOI and actual release date to CITATION.cff.
  3. Confirm that the archive metadata, authors, title, version, and license match the GitHub release.
  4. Preserve the concept DOI for citing the project as a whole and the version DOI for citing this exact release.

The archive step is optional when no archival integration is configured. It must not change the already published tag or silently replace release assets.

docs.title: Tooling & CLI
docs.text:
Copyable examples for the installed console entry points and the public Python API, each checked against the repository's own documentation-example gate.

Source · src/hitop/base/ · src/hitop/suffix/

Prepare the repository once before using the examples below. The bootstrap command creates the local Python environment and installs the HiTOP command-line tools with their dependencies:

scripts/bootstrap_hitop_suffix_tools.sh

docs.title: Generate base-vocabulary codes
docs.text:
Use hitop-codegen to calculate reproducible checksums and complete local HiTOP codes from the maintained base-vocabulary CSV. The command writes a separate generated file, so the curated source data remains unchanged:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-codegen \
  src/data/hitop_base_vocabulary.csv \
  /tmp/hitop_base_vocabulary.generated.csv

Output

Generated 162 HiTOP code(s): /tmp/hitop_base_vocabulary.generated.csv

Inspect the first rows to confirm that the generated file contains the expected columns and code format. This quick check is useful before the file enters further validation or ontology-generation steps:

Command

sed -n '1,5p' /tmp/hitop_base_vocabulary.generated.csv

Output

Code;Label;Segment;Segment Level;CheckDigit;HiTOP
01;Conversion;C;0;qy;C001qy
02;Somatization;C;0;17;C00217
03;Malaise;C;0;3z;C0033z
04;Head Pain;C;0;16;C00416

The checksum calculation uses HiTOP as a fixed internal input. It is not configurable and is not written to the generated HiTOP column.

docs.title: Build manifestation identifiers
docs.text:
Start by converting a canonical organization identifier into a deterministic namespace token. The same ROR identifier will always produce the same token, allowing records from that namespace to be recognized consistently:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix namespace ROR https://ror.org/00tkfw097

Output

{
  "canonical_identifier": "https://ror.org/00tkfw097",
  "namespace_token": "ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK"
}

Convert a human-readable manifestation label into the normalized slug required by the suffix schema. This removes formatting ambiguity before the label becomes part of an identifier:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix slug "Chronic worry"

Output

{
  "slug": "CHRONIC_WORRY"
}

Combine the base concept, manifestation type, namespace token, and normalized slug into one complete manifestation code. Use this step only after each component has been chosen and normalized according to the specification:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix build-code \
  --hitop U0aB2X \
  --manifestation-type AF \
  --namespace-token ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK \
  --slug CHRONIC_WORRY

Output

{
  "code": "U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY"
}

Validate a completed code before storing or exchanging it. A successful result confirms that its structure and individual components satisfy the manifestation-suffix grammar:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix validate-code \
  U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY

Output

{
  "errors": [],
  "valid": true
}

Use an intentionally invalid example to understand the CLI's machine-readable error response. The trailing shell clause keeps an interactive documentation session running, although the validator correctly returns exit status 1:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix validate-code U0aB2X.M-AF-CHRONIC_WORRY || true

Output

The output contains valid: false; the command exit status is 1.

{
  "errors": [
    "Invalid manifestation code: 'U0aB2X.M-AF-CHRONIC_WORRY'."
  ],
  "valid": false
}

Generate a deterministic disambiguator when two local records would otherwise receive the same slug. The contextual identifiers make the resulting suffix reproducible without introducing a manually assigned counter:

Command

.venv/bin/hitop-suffix disambiguator \
  --namespace-identifier https://ror.org/00tkfw097 \
  --hitop U0aB2X \
  --manifestation-type AF \
  --study-id study-a \
  --instrument instrument-x \
  --item-id item-17 \
  --base-slug CHRONIC_WORRY

Output

{
  "basis": "https://ror.org/00tkfw097|u0ab2x|m|af|study-a|instrument-x|item-17",
  "disambiguator": "FPQNQM",
  "slug": "CHRONIC_WORRY_FPQNQM"
}

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
Call the public Python API when code generation needs to be embedded in another tool or data pipeline. This example calculates the checksum and local HiTOP code for one CSV-like source row:

Example

from hitop.base.hitop import build_hitop_code

row = {"Segment": "C", "Segment Level": "0", "Code": "01"}
check_digit, local_code = build_hitop_code(row, row_number=2)

print(check_digit)
print(local_code)

Output

qy
C001qy

The suffix functions can also be composed directly in Python instead of invoking the CLI. This example generates the namespace and slug before assembling the complete code:

Example

from hitop.suffix import build_code, generate_namespace_token, slugify

namespace = generate_namespace_token("ROR", "https://ror.org/00tkfw097")
slug = slugify("Chronic worry")

print(
    build_code(
        hitop_base_code="U0aB2X",
        manifestation_type="AF",
        namespace_token=namespace,
        slug=slug,
    )
)

Output

U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY

Parse an existing manifestation code when downstream software needs access to its individual semantic components. The returned object exposes the base code, type, namespace, and slug separately:

Example

from hitop.suffix import parse_code

parsed = parse_code("U0aB2X.M-AF-ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK-CHRONIC_WORRY")

print(parsed.hitop_base_code)
print(parsed.manifestation_type)
print(parsed.namespace_token)
print(parsed.slug)

Output

U0aB2X
AF
ROR3J2WQSVQFFIKK
CHRONIC_WORRY

See Build & installation for the release gate commands (local quality gate, ontology conversion, Python matrix) that run these same tools as part of a release, and Validation & quality for how CI runs them.

docs.title: Validation & quality
docs.text:
Automated gates check source code, schemas, factorizations, documentation examples, and generated ontology formats before publication.

Source · .github/workflows/ci.yml · validation/

docs.title: Validation pipeline
docs.text:
1. Install the package from locked constraints on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12.
  2. Compile Python sources and run the regression suite under validation/.
  3. Validate documentation code examples and JSON Schema syntax.
  4. Run Ruff lint and formatting checks.
  5. Build the Python distribution and convert RDF to Turtle and OWL.
  6. Run the ROBOT ontology quality report.
  7. Build and publish this website only after all required jobs succeed.

docs.text:
